summary.headline: Sundrop Brands Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 11% with EBITDA margin near 7.2% ex one-offs and ESOPs; FY26 margin up 270 bps.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated (Sundrop plus Del Monte, shown on a like-for-like basis) revenue growth of 11%, with B2B up 12% and e-commerce up 26%. Gross margin expanded close to 4% year on year, and EBITDA margin reached about 7.2% excluding ESOP and one-off costs (Wage Code related), or roughly INR28 crore. For FY26, consolidated growth was 10%, EBITDA grew about 96%, and margin reached about 5.7% with a 270 bps expansion. Management guided to a 150-225 bps annual margin expansion path, targeting double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29, while Italian olive oil value declines and peanut butter share losses remained the main drags.

segments.name: Sundrop (B2C, Act II popcorn, peanut butter, oats, cereals)
segments.commentary: Sundrop is about 57% of revenue; growth accelerated from 5% in FY25 to 12% in FY26, with Q4 at about 14%. Popcorn grew 12% in volume and 18% in value in Q4; Act II popcorn is now above INR400 crore net sales.

segments.name: Del Monte (B2B-led, culinary, Italian, edible oil)
segments.commentary: Del Monte is about 33% of revenue and grew about 9% in FY26 against 13% earlier. Culinary grew about 11% for the year; Italian olive oil value fell about 5% for the year while volume grew about 16-17%.

segments.name: Premium Staples (edible oil)
segments.commentary: Volume growth rose from 3% for FY26 to about 15% in Q4, with value up about 20% in Q4; growth was helped by lower-grammage price-parity packs launched in Q3 and e-commerce investment.

segments.name: Peanut butter (spreads)
segments.commentary: Still declining, about 7% overall; general trade grew low single digits, but share is being lost in modern trade and e-commerce to low-priced competitors, with a price correction via better sourcing.

guidance_outlook: Margin expansion of roughly 150-225 bps annually; about 100 bps in the next year and a further 150-200 bps in FY28 from merger-related efficiencies, per management.
Management intends to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29.
Italian business expected to return to healthy value growth from Q2 FY27 on a like-for-like basis, supported by a campaign starting Q2.
Peanut butter expected to stop share losses and return to volume growth from Q2 FY27.
Marketing spend to grow ahead of top line, targeting around 8% of revenue over about two years, with 40-60% of margin gains reinvested in growth.
Common ERP integration expected to finish in about 12-14 months (around June-August 2027); harmonisation and efficiency takeouts expected from FY28.
capex_capacity: Sales force automation completed: about 475,000 outlets covered (about 375,000 dedicated field force and about 100,000 via distributors), all on the Bizom mobile platform.
Direct reach of about 4.5-5 lakh outlets for ready-to-eat popcorn; total addressable outlets estimated near 1 million.
Common ERP integration under way across the two organisations, expected in about 12-14 months.
Cost programmes covered manufacturing costs, line efficiency, production planning, logistics and freight, delivering the margin gains.
Around 70+ launches in the last year, contributing about 4% of overall sales.
demand_pricing: Popcorn: Sundrop holds about 80%+ share and is number 1 in ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat; ready-to-cook grew about 8% for FY26 (Q4 about 10-11%); RTE is about 34% of popcorn value and RTC about 66%.
Bigger packs grew about 10 percentage points faster than small packs in RTE; bigger RTC packs are about 6-7% of RTC; INR20/INR30 price points are about 6% of the business.
Olive oil deflation was passed on to consumers; Italian value fell 5% for FY26 while volume rose 16-17%, with Del Monte at about third place in Italy behind Figaro and Borges.
Price cuts in peanut butter were achieved through competitive sourcing rather than margin sacrifice; small consumer packs grew double digits in volume.
Core categories (about 62% of portfolio) are expected to grow about 12-13% this year; gross margin for the food business is about 28-30%, with edible oil about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: How far has integration of Sundrop and Del Monte progressed and what benefits have been captured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two businesses still operate largely independently. Integration so far covers back-end CFA network alignment and early use of Sundrop's distribution to push Del Monte ketchup and mayo in general trade; margin gains came mostly from standalone manufacturing and logistics work, about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger synergy plan, timelines and quantum, and can margins expand 200-250 bps a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 150-225 bps of annual margin expansion, around 200 bps as a midpoint, and about 100 bps in the next year plus 150-200 bps in FY28. ERP integration is due in about 12-14 months, and the coverage strategy in 6-9 months with harmonisation from FY28. Management confirmed the intent to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Italian olive oil business declining and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor, CEO of Del Monte Foods, said the value decline reflects olive oil commodity deflation passed through to consumers, with volume up about 17%; no significant margin deterioration. Price corrections are behind the company, and like-for-like value growth is expected from Q2, with an Italian-origin brand campaign starting in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the peanut butter decline and how will it be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Kumar Sharma said the issue was low-priced entrants in commoditised big packs; the company has re-sourced competitively to match prices and expects volume growth from Q2. Small packs grew double digits in volume, and seven new chocolate and high-protein variants were launched in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How are high-protein peanut butter launches priced against peers, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish Bajaj said introductory discounts are used to drive trial; the product is said to be slightly better on protein. The approach is described as transient, with media and performance marketing supporting new users.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core versus non-core growth and gross margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Core categories are expected to grow about 12-13% this year. Food gross margin is about 4-5 points above the company average (about 25%), so about 30%, and edible oil is about 7-8 points lower, around 20%. Gross margin excludes material, manufacturing, freight and logistics costs.

risks_watch: Italian olive oil value growth must turn positive from Q2 FY27 as management guided; watch volume-to-value conversion.
Peanut butter share loss in modern trade and e-commerce to low-priced and protein-focused players; watch whether Q2 volume growth materialises.
Edible oil and packaging inflation in the last two months were passed on to consumers; watch price elasticity and whether gross margins hold after the GST-linked price cuts.
Margin path depends on 150-225 bps annual expansion and reaching double-digit EBITDA margin by FY29; the merger synergies are back-loaded to FY28.
Marketing spend is set to rise toward 8% of revenue, which could compress near-term margin gains.
Reclassification of about INR6 crore of visibility spend affected reported Q4 advertising figures, so underlying comparisons need care.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, cost-led margin expansion and the multi-year margin roadmap, but more guarded on Italian value and peanut butter recovery, which management pushed to Q2 FY27. Several answers stayed high-level on synergy quantification and pricing, and management referred some questions offline to the Company Secretary.
key_quotes: So net-net, there is almost like a 20% delta impact because of passing the benefit of reduced commodity prices to the consumer
Our ambition will be to grow at least 4% to 5% higher than where we today are.
So somewhere close to 200, that could be a little plus/minus, let's say, 25 to 50 bps here or there also possibly.

growth.why: Management guides core category growth of 12-13% for the year and 150-225 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion toward double-digit margin by FY29, backed mainly by cost programmes, pricing/mix and demand gains (Sundrop Q4 ~14%, Premium Staples volume ~15%), with no new physical capacity additions disclosed and ERP integration not yet complete.
